value.body:
Eval vocabulary to settle in the reorg (after #117 lands). Jack Heart: "is it actually true that every eval job is evaluating a single checkpoint? ... Anytime you're running checkpoint 1 against checkpoint 2, that's in some ways evaluating both of those. ... it's not quite clear to me what it means to group multiple evals or group different evals into a single eval job"; on composed players, "(a)": results attach only to the composition, never split to its checkpoint leaves.
Direction: (1) the match is the unit of fact: players (trees) in, result out, stored once and pooled by player identity. (2) An EvalJob declares which matches to play and how (play, agents, machine); Benchmark and RoundRobin are two generators of the match list. Rename Held() to say it is the generator's per-checkpoint slot, not the evaluated subject, and replace Held().player(ref) with a plain way to seat a fixed checkpoint. (3) What is being evaluated is chosen in the report, for any player; composed players report as wholes. (4) Grouping leaves the author vocabulary: compatible matches share a run (jobs.py _group_key); EvalGroup stays internal. Docs follow. No release.
